source.source: World Squash Singles Rules 2025 V1.2, effective 1 September 2025 (updated 14 June 2025 at the WSF Extraordinary General Meeting)

rules.text: Rule 2.1: the winner of a rally scores 1 point and serves to begin the next rally (point-a-rally scoring).
Rule 2.2: each game is played to 11 points; at 10-all the game continues until one player leads by 2 points.
Rule 2.3: a match is normally the best of 5 games, but may be the best of 3 games.
Rule 4.1: players warm up the ball together for a maximum of 4 minutes and change sides after 2 minutes.
Rule 5.1 to 5.2: the winner of the racket spin serves first; while retaining the serve the server must serve from alternate boxes.

Rule 5.7: a serve is good if the ball is dropped or thrown and struck before touching anything else; at the moment of striking one foot is inside the service box touching no boundary; the ball hits the front wall directly between the service line and the out line (not front and side walls simultaneously); it first bounces in the opposite quarter-court without touching a line unless volleyed; and it is not out.
rules.note: Foot-in-box is partially observable from pose plus court calibration, but ball-to-wall and bounce events need ball tracking; the Brain labels serve attempts, it does not call faults.

rules.text: Rule 5.8: a serve that does not comply with 5.7 is a fault and the receiver wins the rally. A serve that hits the service line, short line, half-court line or any boundary line is a fault.

Rule 6.2: a return is good if struck correctly before bouncing twice, reaches the front wall above the tin and below the out line (directly or via other walls) without first bouncing on the floor or hitting a player, rebounds without touching the tin, and is not out.
Rule 7.1 to 7.3: maximum 1 minute between the end of the warm-up and the start of play; 2 minutes between games; 2 minutes to change damaged equipment including protective eyewear.

Rule 8.1: after a reasonable follow-through a player must make every effort to clear so the opponent has a fair view of the ball, access to it, space for a reasonable swing, and freedom to strike to any part of the front wall.
rules.note: Two-player interference is a refereeing judgement; the Brain can only report inter-player distance and swing extent as context.

rules.text: Rule 8.6: no let if no interference or if the striker could not have made a good return; minimal interference yields no let; a let when the opponent made every effort and the striker could have returned; a stroke when the opponent did not make every effort, or when the striker would have made a winning return.

Rule 8.9: a reasonable swing comprises a reasonable backswing, a strike and a reasonable follow-through, not extending more than necessary; Rule 8.10: an excessive swing that causes interference earns no let.
rules.note: Swing extent is observable from pose and racket tracks and is used as a training-context measurement only.

rules.text: Rule 9: outcomes when the ball hits a player depend on whether it was travelling to the front wall and whether the return would have been good.
Rule 11.1: if the ball breaks during a rally a let is allowed for that rally; Rule 11.10: no let for an unusual bounce.
Rule 13.2: self-inflicted injury allows up to 3 minutes recovery; contributed injury up to 15 minutes; Rule 13.3: self-inflicted blood injury up to 5 minutes.
Rule 14: unacceptable conduct is penalised by the Referee with escalating penalties (conduct warning, stroke, game, match).
Appendix 4: the WSF recommends protective eyewear to an appropriate national standard for all players at all times including the warm-up; mandatory for all WSF-sanctioned doubles and junior events.

Appendix 6: coaching is permitted only in intervals between games; player analysis technology may record, store, transmit and analyse during a match but information may not be retrieved by a player during a match.
rules.note: Governs this product: live cues are a training-session feature; in sanctioned matches the Brain may only record and analyse.

rules.text: After each shot recover toward the T (intersection of the short line and half-court line) from where every corner is reachable.
rules.note: Coaching heuristic widely taught; not a rule of the game.

rules.text: Prepare the racket early (racket head up, shoulders turned toward the side wall) before the ball arrives so the swing is a controlled downswing rather than a rushed hit.
Lunge with the lead knee finishing roughly above the ankle, hip-knee-ankle near a right angle; push back off the lead hip and heel to recover.
Training sessions with the Brain should be solo or with a partner standing outside the swing arc; the system freezes feedback when a second person is ambiguous in frame.
